name: Downer EDI Limited
listing_note: DOW.NZ is a secondary, foreign-exempt NZX listing of an ASX-primary stock (ASX: DOW, ~A$7.7-7.9, market cap ~A$5.1bn). The NZX line is illiquid to the point of showing NZ$0.0000 with zero trades; third-party data feeds (e.g. Yahoo Finance) serve a stale NZ$0.00063 quote last updated 20-Jul-2024, with every subsequent daily bar null. This is a data artefact, not a real price. Any NZ investor buying 'DOW.NZ' is economically buying the ASX-listed, AUD-denominated stock, and valuation, liquidity and currency exposure should all be assessed off the ASX line, not the NZX quote.
overview: Downer EDI is Australasia's largest integrated services and infrastructure contractor, maintaining and building essential infrastructure -- roads, rail rolling stock and transit systems, power, gas, water, telecommunications networks, and government/defence facilities -- across Australia and New Zealand. It operates through three reporting segments (Transport, Energy & Utilities, Facilities) on a portfolio of long-term, largely government and quasi-government contracts. The company reports in AUD with a 30 June fiscal year end, and its primary listing is ASX: DOW; DOW.NZ is a thinly-traded secondary line.

business_model.summary: Downer earns fee/margin income from multi-year operations-and-maintenance and project-delivery contracts with government agencies, utilities and large corporates. Revenue is very large (~A$10.3-10.5bn FY2025) relative to profit -- this is a low-single-digit-margin contracting model where small percentage swings in EBITA margin move earnings materially. Approximately 90% of work-in-hand ($38.2bn at 31-Dec-2025) is government-related and approximately 90% is services (recurring maintenance) rather than one-off construction/capital projects, giving the revenue base a largely recurring, contracted character rather than pure project/transactional risk.

revenue_streams.name: Transport (roads, rail & transit systems, NZ projects incl. Hawkins/CRL/Auckland Airport, rail rolling-stock manufacturing e.g. QTMP)
revenue_streams.trend: stable-to-declining (large NZ projects like CRL rolling off, AU road-agency spend soft, though offset by new NZ state highway alliance wins)

revenue_streams.name: Energy & Utilities (power projects/transmission, gas, water, telecommunications)
revenue_streams.trend: mixed - power/energy transition strong, telco/NBN declining as build-out completes

revenue_streams.name: Facilities (Government/Integrated Facilities Management, Defence Estate Maintenance)

business_model.customer_type: Overwhelmingly B2G/quasi-government (federal, state, defence agencies) and large regulated utilities/corporates (e.g. Chevron, Transurban, Stockland); approximately 90% of work-in-hand is government-related
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly Australia with a material New Zealand transport/roads business; H1-2026 revenue included an AUD ~$41m FX headwind from NZD depreciation, indicating NZD revenue is a meaningful minority

main_competitors: Keolis (rail/transit, formerly a Downer JV partner)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the two or three largest diversified infrastructure-services contractors in Australia/NZ (alongside Ventia and UGL); leading position in road maintenance and rail services in Australasia and a top-tier defence facilities contractor

moat_factors.description: Long-dated maintenance contracts (often 5-10 years) on essential infrastructure create high switching costs for government customers, embedded local knowledge, plant and workforce; re-tendering cycles are, however, a recurring source of both risk and opportunity
$1.9bn of performance bonding facilities and a Fitch BBB issuer rating give Downer capacity to bid and be awarded large multi-year government contracts that smaller players cannot bond
Exposure spread across roads, rail, power, water, telco and defence facilities reduces single-sector cyclicality versus pure-play peers

Reputation was materially damaged by the FY2023 accounting scandal and subsequent regulatory/legal actions; being rebuilt under new management but remains a headwind in competitive tenders and financing costs

weaknesses: Structurally thin margins (underlying EBITA margin only 4.6% in 1H26, described as best in a decade) leave very little buffer against cost overruns or contract mispricing

Heavy reliance on government tendering cycles and public infrastructure/agency budgets that can be cut or delayed by political change (e.g. softer Australian state Transport agency spend cited repeatedly in FY25/1H26)

History of poor contract risk management (the FY2023 Utilities WIP/revenue-recognition scandal, and multiple 'underperforming contracts' exited in FY25/1H26) suggests execution and internal-control risk is not yet fully remediated
Labour- and subcontractor-intensive cost base (subcontractor costs ~42% and employee costs ~31% of the ~$4.7bn 1H26 cost base) exposes margins to wage inflation and subcontractor availability

growth_drivers: Energy transition-related capex: transmission line and substation construction within Power Projects is a clear structural growth pocket, offsetting the winding-down of NBN telco build-out work

Defence spending growth: new Defence Property and Asset Services (PAS) contract ($3.05bn, awarded Sept-2025, commenced Feb-2026) and Defence Professional Services contract ($220m) reflect rising Australian defence budgets and infrastructure needs

Portfolio simplification/margin mix shift: completed divestment of low-margin Cleaning, Catering and Laundries businesses and the Keolis Downer JV stake has structurally lifted group EBITA margin (4.6% in 1H26 vs 3.7% in 1H25) by removing dilutive, higher-risk revenue

Work-in-hand growth: total work-in-hand rose 8.9% to $38.2bn at 31-Dec-2025 on the back of the PAS contract, a $750m Chevron maintenance contract, an Urban Utilities water/wastewater contract, and other renewals -- a strong forward indicator even as reported revenue has declined

New Zealand State Highway contracts: preferred-bidder status on NZD$870m of NZ state highway maintenance contracts, plus a firm NZD$311m Project Alliance Agreement (2NL South Alliance, Otaki-to-North-of-Levin highway, awarded Aug-2025) -- a confirmed tailwind for the currently soft NZ Transport business

Capital return: the A$230m on-market buyback (~5% of issued capital, launched 21-Aug-2025, running to 30-Jun-2026; ~12.4m of 671.6m shares on issue repurchased by mid-2026) is accretive to EPS and signals management/board confidence in free cash generation

Diversification beyond pure-government Facilities customers: new A$500m, five-year Integrated Facilities Management contract with Stockland (commencing 1-Aug-2026) and a A$310m Transurban Sydney motorway maintenance contract broaden the private-sector customer base

Continued cost-out and operating-model simplification (technology/shared-services consolidation) supporting further margin expansion toward and above the group's stated 5% underlying EBITDA margin floor

business.description: Large single contracts (e.g. a Victorian power maintenance contract not renewed in July 2025, the EMOS-to-PAS Defence transition causing a margin reset in 2H26) show that loss or unfavourable renegotiation of any major contract can swing group earnings meaningfully given thin overall margins

At a ~4-5% underlying EBITA margin, cost overruns, weather disruption or a handful of mispriced contracts can erase a large share of group profit, as demonstrated by the FY2023 scandal and repeated 'underperforming contract' exits through FY25/1H26

business.risk: New Zealand and Australian Transport softness
business.description: Australian Road Services volumes remain impacted by reduced state Transport agency spend, and large NZ projects (City Rail Link, Auckland Airport) are rolling off with softer near-term replacement activity, though this is partially offset by new NZ state highway maintenance and alliance wins

financial.description: A$400m bridge facility in place ahead of an AUD MTN refinancing due in FY26; Fitch affirmed BBB in Feb-2026 but the rating explicitly depends on maintaining underlying EBITDA margin above a 5% covenant-style threshold
NZD-denominated revenue translated into AUD reporting currency created a ~$41m revenue headwind in 1H26 alone from NZD depreciation

financial.risk: Leverage headroom is currently comfortable but capital is being returned aggressively
financial.description: Net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.8x at Dec-2025 from 1.3x a year earlier, but the $230m buyback plus dividends (payout ratio raised to 65%, though the trailing dividend yield of ~2.2% is below the 5-year average of ~3.7% as the raised payout has not fully offset a lower share count/rebased base) reduces the cushion available if earnings disappoint

regulatory.description: A consolidated Victorian Supreme Court class action (Maurice Blackburn lead, Piper Alderman/other firms also involved) alleges Downer misled the market over FY20-23 Utilities revenue/WIP misreporting, covering shareholders who acquired stock between 23-Jul-2019 and 24-Feb-2023. Registration deadline for group members closed 10-Sep-2025; a court-ordered mediation was scheduled to commence by 12-Dec-2025. Downer has cross-claimed against former auditor KPMG, which resigned as auditor as a result, and KPMG was separately joined as a direct defendant by plaintiffs in Feb-2025 (with KPMG filing a third-party claim back against Downer in May-2025). As of this analysis (Aug-2026), no public confirmation of a settlement or mediation outcome has been located -- the matter remains a live, unresolved contingent liability disclosed in the FY/HY accounts, and if unsettled would be expected to proceed toward trial.

In December 2024 the ACCC commenced Federal Court civil cartel proceedings against Downer subsidiary Spotless Facility Services and Ventia Australia (together with related allegations involving BGIS) and four senior executives, alleging price-fixing arrangements on three occasions between April 2019 and August 2022 relating to Defence estate maintenance/operation services (including a COVID-era SME stimulus work program). The ACCC is seeking penalties, costs and disqualification orders against three executives. Downer 'categorically denies' the allegations and is vigorously defending. As of Aug-2026 the case remains in the Federal Court with no penalty, ruling or settlement publicly confirmed; this is separate from, and in addition to, the shareholder class action, and both continue to generate 'regulatory reviews and legal matters' costs each half (A$6.3m pre-tax in 1H26 alone).

Heightened regulator and customer scrutiny following the accounting scandal and ACCC action increases the risk of exclusion from, or added compliance cost in, future government tenders -- though Downer continued to win large new Defence and government contracts (PAS, Defence Professional Services) through the case's pendency, suggesting limited practical tendering impact so far

macro.description: Revenue is ~90% government-related; state and federal budget tightening, election cycles or shifts in infrastructure priorities directly affect contract volumes, as already seen in soft AU Transport agency spend

Employee benefits (~31%) and subcontractor costs (~42%) are the two largest cost lines; wage inflation or skilled-labour shortages in Australia/NZ construction and utilities markets pressure margins directly
Management's own FY26 guidance is explicitly conditioned on 'no material weather disruptions,' underscoring seasonal/climate risk to outdoor infrastructure work
Net finance costs already a meaningful P&L line (A$34.2m in 1H26); rate moves affect refinancing cost on the upcoming AUD MTN and the group's ~A$242m net debt plus lease liabilities

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Positive structural demand from the energy transition (transmission/substation build-out), rising Australian defence spending, and population-growth-driven infrastructure and utilities investment; offset by a mature/completing NBN telecommunications cycle and cautious state government transport-agency budgets
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Recurring maintenance work (~90% of work-in-hand) smooths some cyclicality, but project-delivery revenue (major rail/transit builds, road construction) is more cyclical and tied to public capex cycles and election-driven budget decisions
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via financing costs and via government capex appetite; direct balance-sheet sensitivity is currently modest given improved leverage (0.8x net debt/EBITDA)
key_input_costs: Steel/raw materials and consumables for rail and infrastructure builds

recent_developments.event: FY2025 result (reported 21-Aug-2025): statutory NPAT of $149.1m (+82% YoY), underlying EBITDA margin 4.4% (highest in over a decade), final dividend 14.1cps fully franked (65% payout), and announcement of a A$230m on-market buyback (~5% of issued capital)

Downer's alliance (2NL South Alliance) awarded a firm NZD$311m Project Alliance Agreement to construct the southern section of the Otaki-to-North-of-Levin highway for NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi, following a 12-month+ interim alliance phase
On-market buyback formally commenced 16-Sep-2025 (notification lodged 21-Aug-2025), targeting up to A$230m and running through 30-Jun-2026, executed via Macquarie Securities

Registration deadline (10-Sep-2025) closed for group members in the consolidated shareholder class action over the FY20-23 accounting irregularities, covering shareholders who acquired stock 23-Jul-2019 to 24-Feb-2023
Defence Property and Asset Services (PAS) contract awarded, worth A$3.05bn, commencing operations 1-Feb-2026 and replacing the prior EMOS Defence base-services arrangement
Won ~NZD$870m of New Zealand state highway maintenance contracts (preferred-contractor status, alongside the confirmed 2NL South Alliance agreement) -- a material NZ Transport tailwind

Completed sale of remaining 49% interest in Keolis Downer transit JV to Keolis Group (completed 1-Dec-2025), finalising Downer's exit from that rail/transit JV and booking a small net gain plus a A$23.9m pre-completion dividend

Court-ordered mediation in the shareholder class action was scheduled to commence by 12-Dec-2025 (Supreme Court of Victoria); no public confirmation of a settlement or outcome has been located as of Aug-2026 -- treated as unresolved

H1-2026 (half year to 31-Dec-2025) result: statutory NPAT $98.0m (+30%), underlying NPATA $136.1m (+7.0%), underlying EBITA margin improved to 4.6% (from 3.7%), work-in-hand up 8.9% to $38.2bn, net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.8x from 1.3x, interim dividend raised 19% to 12.9cps (100% franked); Fitch reaffirmed BBB issuer rating

FY2026 underlying guidance issued: revenue slightly lower than FY25 pro forma revenue, further EBITA margin improvement, and underlying NPATA of $295m-$315m, conditional on no material change in economic conditions/demand and no material weather disruption

Secured a new A$310m contract with Transurban to maintain Sydney's motorway network, and a new A$500m, five-year Integrated Facilities Management contract with Stockland commencing 1-Aug-2026, both evidencing growth in private-sector (non-government) customer wins

On-market buyback progress update: approximately 12.44m shares repurchased cumulatively (of the A$230m/~5% program) against 671.57m shares on issue, with the buyback continuing on a near-daily basis toward its 30-Jun-2026 scheduled end

ACCC Federal Court civil cartel proceedings against Downer subsidiary Spotless (and Ventia, with related BGIS allegations) over alleged 2019-2022 Defence estate-maintenance price-fixing remain ongoing and unresolved as of Aug-2026; Downer continues to deny the allegations and defend the case, with no penalty or settlement publicly confirmed

FY2026 full-year result (year to 30-Jun-2026) has NOT yet been released as of this analysis (10-Aug-2026); Downer's investor calendar shows the FY26 results briefing scheduled for 20-Aug-2026, with the AGM to follow on 11-Nov-2026. Actual results versus the $295-315m underlying NPATA guidance are not yet known

guidance.as_of: H1-2026 Results, 19 February 2026 (FY2026 full-year result due 20-Aug-2026, not yet reported as of this analysis)

items.target: Slightly lower than FY25 pro forma revenue of $10.348bn (adjusted for the 1H26 E&U customer-contract disposal)
items.notes: Reflects continued shedding of low-margin/divested revenue rather than underlying volume weakness; not yet confirmed against actuals pending 20-Aug-2026 result

items.vs_prior: raised (continuation of the multi-year margin-recovery trend)
items.notes: Management explicitly tracks a minimum 5% underlying EBITDA margin threshold tied to the Fitch BBB rating

items.vs_prior: new range provided at H1-2026; implies continued double-digit-percentage growth versus FY25 underlying NPATA
items.notes: Explicitly conditioned on no material change in economic conditions or market demand, and no material weather disruptions; no updated/reaffirmed guidance has been issued since Feb-2026 as the full-year result (due 20-Aug-2026) has not yet occurred
1H26 normalised cash conversion of 90.5% exceeded this target

items.target: No explicit numeric target disclosed but trending toward further improvement
items.notes: Improved to 0.8x at 31-Dec-2025 from 1.3x a year earlier; management commentary frames this as capacity to invest and pursue growth, including continuing the buyback

guidance.management_commentary: Management (CEO Peter Tompkins) characterised 1H26 performance as 'in line with expectations,' attributing improvement to tighter tendering risk guardrails, completion/renegotiation of underperforming contracts, and the benefits of portfolio simplification (exit of low-margin Cleaning, Catering, Laundries and the Keolis Downer JV). The Board highlighted work-in-hand growth of 8.9% to $38.2bn as evidence of expanding medium-term growth positioning, while flagging that the Defence PAS contract margin will reset lower in 2H26 during transition from the prior EMOS arrangement, and that NZ Transport and Australian Road Services volumes remain soft near-term (though partly offset by the new NZ state highway contract wins). No further formal guidance update has been issued since the 19-Feb-2026 H1 result; the market awaits the FY2026 result on 20-Aug-2026 to see whether the $295-315m underlying NPATA range is met.

bull_case: Genuine, multi-year margin turnaround is visible and continuing in the numbers: underlying EBITA margin has risen from 2.9% (1H25 statutory) to 4.6% (1H26 underlying) largely from portfolio simplification and cost discipline, with FY26 guidance calling for further improvement and NPATA of $295-315m (result due 20-Aug-2026)

Balance sheet has been meaningfully repaired -- net debt/EBITDA down to 0.8x from 1.3x, a Fitch BBB rating reaffirmed, and $2.3bn of liquidity -- giving room for the A$230m buyback (~5% of shares, ~12.4m of 671.6m shares repurchased by mid-2026) plus a growing, now fully-franked dividend (65% payout) without straining the balance sheet

~90% government-related, ~90% services work-in-hand ($38.2bn, +8.9% in the half) provides revenue visibility and recurring-style economics uncommon for a construction/contracting business, underpinned by structural tailwinds in defence spend, the energy transition, and confirmed new NZ highway contracts (NZD$870m preferred-bidder status plus a firm NZD$311m alliance agreement)

Divestment program (Laundries, Catering, Cleaning, Keolis Downer, Australian Transport Projects) has removed the lowest-margin, highest-risk parts of the portfolio, and new private-sector wins (Stockland A$500m IFM, Transurban A$310m) show the recovering business can win work beyond government customers

Valuation is not obviously stretched -- consensus analyst rating is broadly Hold with price targets (~A$8.23-8.25) only modestly above the recent A$7.7-7.9 share price, suggesting the market has not yet fully re-rated the turnaround if margin gains prove durable, and neither major legal overhang has yet crystallised a negative outcome
bear_case: Two significant unresolved legal/regulatory overhangs -- the consolidated shareholder class action over FY20-23 accounting irregularities (mediation scheduled Dec-2025, no settlement or outcome publicly confirmed as of Aug-2026) and the ACCC Federal Court price-fixing proceedings against Spotless (alongside Ventia, with related BGIS allegations) over Defence estate-maintenance contracts -- create binary tail risk to both cash and reputation that remains fully live, with no resolution date visible

Margins remain structurally thin (~4-5% EBITA) in a labour- and subcontractor-heavy business, meaning the current 'turnaround' could as easily reverse on a handful of mispriced contracts as it improved from disciplined exits -- the FY2023 scandal itself began as contract-level misreporting

Core Transport segment still faces headwinds: large NZ projects (City Rail Link, Auckland Airport terminal) are nearing completion, Australian road-agency spend remains soft, and Hawkins is deliberately shrinking through disciplined project selection; new NZ highway wins only partially offset this and are not yet reflected in reported revenue

Government-contract concentration cuts both ways: the loss of a Victorian power maintenance contract and the EMOS-to-PAS Defence transition margin reset in 2H26 show how quickly a single large contract change can swing segment earnings, and ~90% government exposure leaves the business fully at the mercy of public infrastructure budget cycles

The dividend yield (~2.2%) is currently below its 5-year average (~3.7%) despite a raised payout ratio, and the FY2026 full-year result (due 20-Aug-2026, not yet released as of this analysis) is a near-term binary catalyst against a guidance range that already assumes no weather disruption and stable economic conditions

The DOW.NZ line itself is effectively untradeable/illiquid, meaning any NZ-domiciled holder is really underwriting ASX-line, AUD-denominated risk and currency exposure while getting none of the liquidity benefit of a real local market -- a structural, non-fundamental risk specific to accessing this name via the NZX ticker
